q: How many sharps are in the key of D major?
why: D major has F sharp and C sharp. Fiddle players live here.

q: In D Dorian (parent key C), what Roman numeral is the home chord?
why: Numerals count from the parent major key. D Dorian's home chord is the ii of C.

why: Elvis Presley carried the title from the 1950s on.

q: How many eighth notes fit in one whole note?
why: A whole note is 4 beats in 4/4; an eighth is half a beat. 4 times 2 is 8.

q: At 120 BPM, how long is one quarter-note beat?
why: 60 seconds divided by 120 beats is half a second each.

q: What is the name of the therapy that uses music to help health?
why: Music therapy is a licensed clinical field.

q: Which part of the ear turns vibrations into nerve signals?
why: Hair cells in the cochlea fire the auditory nerve.

q: What is the unit for how many vibrations happen per second?
why: Hertz counts cycles per second. A4 is 440 Hz.

q: If you go up an octave, what happens to the frequency?
why: A4 is 440 Hz, A5 is 880 Hz.

q: How many keys does a standard piano have?
why: 52 white and 36 black.

q: Which instrument family does the saxophone belong to?
why: It is made of brass but uses a reed, so it is a woodwind.

q: Which composer wrote the Moonlight Sonata?
why: Beethoven, Piano Sonata No. 14. The nickname came later from a critic.

why: Beethoven wrote his Ninth Symphony while almost fully deaf.

why: Satchmo on trumpet, plus that famous gravel voice.

q: How many bars long is a standard blues form?
why: The 12-bar blues: I, IV and V spread over twelve bars.

q: Which country does the sitar come from?
why: The sitar is a plucked string instrument from northern India.

why: Samba grew up in Rio de Janeiro.
